summary: Tells the boot process which deployment (image version) to start.
Where the root filesystem is.
Mount options for the root filesystem, for example the btrfs subvolume.
Filesystem type of the root filesystem.
Mounts the root filesystem read-write at start so the system can set up its own read-only view.
Unlocks the encrypted disk with the TPM automatically. Without it you type the disk passphrase at every boot.
risk: The system still boots, but asks for the passphrase.

summary: Disk-encryption unlock settings read before the system starts. Removing one can leave the disk locked.
Tells early boot which LVM volumes to activate.
Tells early boot which software RAID to assemble.
Early-boot device-mapper settings.
Disk-encryption unlock settings. Removing one can leave the disk locked.
Hides most boot messages.
Shows a splash screen during boot.
Graphical boot screen.
Mounts the root filesystem read-only at start.
Where to resume from after hibernation.
risk: Removing it disables hibernation.

summary: Offset of the hibernation file inside the resume device.
risk: Removing it can break hibernation.

summary: Turns off the kernel graphics drivers; the screen runs in a basic, slow mode.
risk: Usually only for troubleshooting.

summary: Where kernel messages are shown.
Forces a screen mode or output setting.
Uses the AMD P-State driver in active mode to control CPU frequency.
Unlocks all AMD GPU power features. Needed for overclocking, undervolting and fan control tools such as LACT.
risk: Lets tools set clocks and voltages that can crash the GPU or damage it if misused.

summary: Lets the kernel reset a hung AMD GPU instead of freezing the machine.
Stops the kernel from slowing programs that do misaligned atomic operations. Some games depend on this.
Turns off the hardware watchdog timers. Saves a little power and fewer wake-ups.
Turns off the NMI watchdog, a lockup detector. Saves a little power.
Turns off CPU security mitigations (Spectre, Meltdown and others). Faster, but weaker protection.
risk: Programs you run, including web pages, can attack the system more easily.

summary: Keeps the Magic SysRq key combinations usable for emergencies, such as a safe reboot.
Never powers down idle USB devices. Avoids dropped controllers and dongles; uses a little more power.
Uses the IOMMU in passthrough mode: fast for normal use, still available for virtual machines.
Fully preemptible kernel scheduling: lower latency, slightly lower throughput.
Uses large memory pages only for programs that ask for them.
Sets how aggressively the kernel defragments memory for large pages, to avoid stalls.
Ignores unknown CPU registers in virtual machines. Avoids crashes in some guests.
risk: Lets guests that read CPU registers the host does not expose (some Windows guests) keep running instead of crashing. Only useful if you run virtual machines.

summary: Does not log the ignored register accesses.
risk: Lets guests that read CPU registers the host does not expose (some Windows guests) keep running instead of crashing. Only useful if you run virtual machines.

summary: Turns off PCIe link power saving. Avoids hangs on some hardware; uses more power at idle.
risk: Fixes dropped connections on Intel igc Ethernet controllers. Raises idle power use on every PCIe device, not only the network card.

summary: Staggers the timer tick across CPUs, which can reduce latency spikes.
Hides the UMIP CPU feature so some older Windows games and Wine programs run.
Lets drivers, for example fan and sensor tools, use hardware that the firmware also claims.
Turn off NVMe power-state switching (APST).
risk: Uses a little more power when idle. Helps SSDs that freeze, disappear or throw errors under load, which is a known problem on some laptops.

summary: Use deep sleep (S3) instead of s2idle when suspending.
risk: If this machine's firmware has no deep sleep, suspend can fail or the system may not wake up. Many newer laptops and handhelds only support s2idle. Test suspend and resume after enabling.

summary: Run interrupt handlers as threads.
risk: Can lower audio and input latency under heavy load. May slightly reduce throughput; rarely a driver misbehaves.

summary: Turn off scatter-gather display on AMD graphics.
risk: Fixes flickering or a blank screen on some AMD laptops and handhelds. Costs a little memory bandwidth. Only useful with AMD graphics.

summary: Turn off Panel Self Refresh on Intel graphics.
risk: Fixes flicker or screen freezes on some Intel laptop panels. Uses a little more power. Only useful with Intel graphics.

summary: Hide PCIe Advanced Error Reporting messages.
risk: Stops PCIe error messages from flooding the log. Real hardware problems on the PCIe bus will no longer be reported, which makes them harder to diagnose.

summary: Poll USB mice 1000 times a second.
risk: Lowers input latency for gaming mice. Uses slightly more CPU time, and a few very old mice misbehave.

summary: Keep an AMD graphics card powered instead of letting it sleep.
risk: Fixes black screens and hangs after idle on some desktops and laptops. Uses more power at idle. Only useful with AMD graphics.

summary: Turn on Nvidia kernel mode setting.
risk: Needed for Wayland and tear-free output on older Nvidia drivers; newer drivers may already enable it. Only useful with the Nvidia driver.

summary: Turn on the Intel IOMMU (for passing devices to virtual machines).
risk: Needed to give a graphics card or other device to a virtual machine. Can cause problems with some devices and costs a little speed. Only useful on Intel CPUs.

summary: Rotates the built-in portrait panel so the screen is upright.
risk: Only matches the ONEXPLAYER F1 and F1 EVA-01. Switching it off turns the boot screen sideways again.

summary: Starts the boot splash on the real graphics driver instead of the simple framebuffer.
risk: Only matches the ONEXPLAYER F1 and F1 EVA-01. Switching it off turns the boot screen sideways again.

summary: Hides kernel messages during boot.
risk: Only matches the ONEXPLAYER F1 and F1 EVA-01. Switching it off turns the boot screen sideways again.

summary: Makes the kernel strict about ACPI resource conflicts.
risk: Stops random reboots on the AYANEO SLIDE. Only matches that model.

summary: Stops the hid_sensor_hub module from loading, which fixes the keyboard.
risk: Screen auto-rotation and ambient light sensors that use that module stop working. Only matches Framework laptops with Intel in the model name.

summary: Turns off Panel Self Refresh in the AMD display driver.
risk: Fixes flicker or artifacts on some AMD laptop and handheld panels. The display stays in a higher-power state, so battery life drops. Some panels need a different value than this one. Only useful with AMD graphics.

summary: Turns on extra display features in the AMD driver (HDMI 2.1 and FreeSync).
risk: Bazzite offers this for HDMI 2.1 and FreeSync over HDMI. It can cause flicker or instability on some displays. Only useful with AMD graphics.

summary: Turns off the deepest display power-saving states on Intel graphics.
risk: Avoids random reboots or failed suspend on Intel graphics from about 2012 to 2015. Uses more power while the screen is idle. Only useful with Intel graphics.

summary: Lets the Nvidia driver provide the framebuffer console.
risk: Helps some Nvidia setups keep a working console and resume from sleep. Experimental in the driver. Only useful with the Nvidia driver.

summary: Saves video memory contents when the system sleeps.
risk: Fixes a black or corrupted screen after resume on some Nvidia setups. Needs the nvidia-suspend, nvidia-resume and nvidia-hibernate services to be enabled. Only useful with the Nvidia driver.

summary: Sets the PCIe power policy to performance.
risk: Fixes dropped connections on Intel igc Ethernet controllers. Raises idle power use on every PCIe device, not only the network card.

summary: Stops the kernel from powering down PCIe ports.
risk: Fixes devices that disappear or hang after sleep on some boards. Raises idle power use.

summary: Uses s2idle (light sleep) when suspending.
risk: For machines that fail to wake from deep sleep. s2idle uses more battery while asleep. The opposite of the deep sleep preset; switch on only one.
